findings.title: Toward Effective and Reliable LLM Agents via Dynamic Ontology (OaK: Ontology-as-a-Kernel)
findings.key_findings: Introduces OaK (Ontology-as-a-Kernel), a framework that dynamically constructs task-oriented ontologies for LLM agents. The kernel K=(S,F) couples a task-oriented schema S (defining domain concepts, properties, relations) with a catalog of typed reasoning functions F (retrieval, filtering, traversal, projection, aggregation, multi-step reasoning). During construction, OaK instantiates a schema-guided knowledge graph from task data, then uses judge-driven refinement (official task scores + execution trajectories) to iteratively repair schema and functions before freezing the kernel for inference. Evaluated on TravelPlanner, CRMArenaPro, ToolQA — consistent gains across DeepSeek-v4-flash and GPT-4o-mini backbones. Ablation confirms function composition, function module, and iterative refinement are critical. This operationalizes ontology as an executable interface (semantic + procedural contract) rather than a passive description.

findings.title: DIAL-KG: Schema-Free Incremental Knowledge Graph Construction via Dynamic Schema Induction and Evolution-Intent Assessment
findings.key_findings: Closed-loop incremental KG construction orchestrated by a Meta-Knowledge Base (MKB). Three-stage cycle per batch: (1) Dual-Track Extraction — defaults to triple generation, switches to event extraction for complex n-ary/time-varying knowledge; (2) Governance Adjudication — evidence verification, consistency checks, intent recognition (Informational vs Evolutionary), auditable soft deprecation as transactional updates; (3) Schema Evolution — new schemas induced from validated knowledge guide subsequent cycles, knowledge incrementally applied to existing KG. Achieves SOTA on both graph quality and induced schema quality: +4.7% F1 over schema-free LLM baselines, >98% precision on evidence-backed soft deprecations, 15% fewer relation types, 1.6–2.8 point redundancy reduction. MKB serves as both governance hub and evolutionary memory with versioned entity profiles and schema proposals.

findings.title: Evo-DKD: Dual-Knowledge Decoding for Autonomous Ontology Evolution in Large Language Models
findings.key_findings: Dual-decoder architecture inside LLM: one decoder stream produces structured ontology edits (class insertions, relation assertions, schema modifications), the other produces unstructured natural-language explanations/reasoning. Dynamic attention-based gating mechanism coordinates the two streams at each generation step. Closed-loop autonomous updating: proposed edits validated via consistency checks (structured KB constraints) and cross-verification with text explanations, then injected into KB which informs subsequent reasoning. Evaluated on healthcare ontology refinement, semantic search improvement, cultural heritage timeline modeling. Full Dual-Decoder mode outperforms structured-only and unstructured-only baselines on triple extraction accuracy (Exact/Relaxed Match), explanation quality (BLEU, BERTScore), and LLM-Judge reliability score. Current implementation simulates dual-decoder via prompt-based mode control; future work targets dedicated trained decoders with dynamic gating.

findings.title: DySECT: A Dynamic Self-Evolving Extraction and Curation Toolkit
findings.key_findings: Closed-loop IE system where extraction continuously improves knowledge and knowledge continuously improves extraction. Three components: (1) Extraction Step — LLM produces concept-level triples from raw text; (2) KB Growth — nested loops: outer loop ingests extractor batches, inner loop performs knowledge integration (hierarchical clustering via KNN+LLM for concept abstractions, mutual-exclusivity reasoning, probabilistic confidence aggregation via noisy-or with shrinkage factor λ=0.75), concept acquisition (instance discovery), relation acquisition (fact discovery); (3) Feedback Mechanisms — KB knowledge re-injected into extractor via prompt augmentation (KB-informed few-shot examples), KB-informed concept abstractions, or synthetic data for lightweight fine-tuning. Uses Theo KB library with continuous expansion and reliability estimation. Improves recall 5-8% on DocRED across GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, LLaMA-3.3-70B, Kimi K2.5 without fine-tuning. GitHub: github.com/megagonlabs/dysect.

findings.title: DSE-RE: Dynamic Schema Evolution with LLM for Iterative Relation Extraction
findings.key_findings: Framework that dynamically adapts to diverse domains for iterative relation extraction and KG construction. Integrates schema evolution directly into LLM prompts — the schema evolves as the system processes new documents, with LLM proposing schema modifications (new relations, type constraints) validated against extraction consistency. Iterative loop: extract relations → detect schema gaps/conflicts → LLM proposes schema updates → validate → update schema → repeat. Addresses the fundamental problem that fixed schemas fail on evolving domains. Published in Human-Centric Intelligent Systems, DOI: 10.1007/s44230-026-00158-1.

findings.title: OntoRipple: Making Waves in the Knowledge Graph Lifecycle (Ontology Change Propagation)
findings.key_findings: Automates propagation of ontology changes into RML mappings and SHACL shapes to construct and validate KGs, ensuring consistency with evolving ontology in a fully declarative workflow. Supports 25 distinct change operations from OWL Change Ontology covering classes, properties, class/property relations, property characteristics. Change Propagation Engine processes changes in predefined dependency order (e.g., AddClass before AddSubClass). When assumptions needed for propagation, modified triples flagged for user review. GitHub: github.com/oeg-upm/OntoRipple. Complementary work: OCP2KG framework (CEUR-WS 2024) for declarative change description and propagation over mapping rules.

findings.title: ATOM: AdapTive and OptiMized Dynamic Temporal Knowledge Graph Construction Using LLMs
findings.key_findings: Few-shot scalable approach for building and continuously updating Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) from unstructured text. Three-module parallel pipeline: (1) Atomic Fact Decomposition — splits documents into minimal self-contained 'atomic facts' to address LLM forgetting in long contexts; (2) Dual-Time Modeling — distinguishes observation time (when system learned) from validity time (when fact true in world), constructs atomic TKGs with 5-tuples (quintuples); (3) Parallel Merge — merges atomic TKGs. Achieves ~18% higher exhaustivity, ~33% better stability, >90% latency reduction vs baselines. Evolved from iText2KG (incremental KG construction). GitHub: github.com/AuvaLab/itext2kg.

findings.title: Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents (Versioned Memory Graphs)
findings.key_findings: Formal belief revision semantics for versioned memory architectures. Addresses the gap: individual components (versioning, retrieval, consolidation) exist in Graphiti, Mem0, Letta, but architectural synthesis and formal grounding underexplored. Introduces graph-native cognitive memory with immutable revisions and typed reasoning edges. Letta Context Repositories (Feb 2026) use git-backed memory filesystems with automatic versioning and merge-based conflict resolution via multi-agent worktrees — but use Git (source code versioning) pragmatically as storage for Markdown. The proposed versioned memory graph provides: formal belief revision, auditability, traceability for regulatory compliance (SOX 404, HIPAA, GDPR, EU AI Act Art. 12). Enterprise memory graph market: Zylos Research (Feb 2026) reports 65% of enterprise AI failures in 2025 due to context drift/memory loss.

findings.title: EOAC-LLM: An LLM-Driven Event Ontology Automatic Construction System
findings.venue: Intelligent Systems with Applications, Vol 30, Article 200650 (March 2026)
findings.key_findings: Full-process automated framework for event ontology construction eliminating manual annotation. Five core modules: (1) Event ontology modeling corpus generation; (2) Event element-relation extraction; (3) Deep semantic representation and aggregation — multi-dimensional dynamic aggregation for semantic-temporal-relation with dynamic weighting; (4) Event ontology generation; (5) Dynamic update — event gap identification and incremental update mechanism for self-driven dynamic evolution. Temporal relation-aware hierarchical clustering with temporal consistency scoring addresses uneven cluster granularity. Validated in emergency disaster relief domain with Deepseek, Doubao, ERNIE Bot — outperforms baselines. DOI: 10.1016/j.iswa.2026.200650.

findings.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory / Graphiti
findings.key_findings: Temporal knowledge graphs as agent memory layer. Bi-temporal model tracks valid time (true in world) and ingestion/provenance time; superseded facts invalidated not deleted. Graphiti (getzep/graphiti, ~30k stars, Apache-2.0) is real-time incremental bi-temporal KG engine with MCP server for Claude/Cursor. Edges include explicit validity intervals (t_valid, t_invalid). Semantic, keyword, graph search for conflict detection; temporal metadata used to update/invalidate outdated info preserving history. Powers Zep's Context Lake (millions of graphs, sub-200ms p95). Key differentiator from GraphRAG: continuous incremental updates vs batch; temporal context graph with episodes, communities vs entity clusters; hybrid search vs sequential LLM summarization. Cognee (topoteretes/cognee) adds ECL pipeline (Extract, Cognify, Load) on dlt framework with hybrid Neo4j/Kuzu + pgvector/LanceDB.

findings.title: OntoEKG: LLM-Driven Ontology Construction for Enterprise Knowledge Graphs
findings.key_findings: Two-phase pipeline for enterprise ontology construction from unstructured text: (1) Ontological Element Extraction — identifies classes and properties with Pydantic-enforced JSON output; (2) Hierarchy Construction with Entailment — Entailment LLM iteratively analyzes extracted classes to determine inheritance relationships (subsumption) using logical reasoning on class descriptions; (3) RDF Serialization via rdflib to Turtle. Evaluated on Data/Finance/Logistics sectors — fuzzy-match F1 0.724 on Data domain. Identifies limitations: scope definition difficulty, LLM proposes individuals instead of classes, hierarchy directionality confusion, loose subsumption definitions. Calls for comprehensive benchmark for end-to-end ontology construction from text (existing benchmarks like OntoURL, Text2KGBench, LLMs4OL are incomplete for this task).

findings.title: SCOPE and SCION: Benchmark and Auditable Pipeline for Corpus-to-Schema Induction
findings.key_findings: SCOPE — train-text-only benchmark for corpus-to-schema induction and optional schema fusion from raw text, built from 24 public IE sources (15 RE, 9 EE) normalized into gold schema graphs. SCION — auditable reference pipeline (not new extraction architecture) that constructs candidate spaces from train text and restricts naming, merging, filtering, validation, conservative fusion to candidate-linked evidence under strict JSON contracts. SCION-lite attains highest F1 among released source-schema references, Text2Onto-style, LLM-only, and matched extract-then-aggregate baselines under Literal, Fuzzy, Continuous, Graph schema-graph metrics. Addresses upstream bottleneck: most extraction systems assume schema available, but schema graphs are the actual bottleneck.

findings.title: Living Databases: A Unified Model for Continuous Schema Evolution, Versioning, and Transformations
findings.key_findings: Unified model for continuous schema evolution with versioning and transformations. Supports sandboxing for development/testing/migrations without impacting production; alternate 'what-if' realities for scenario planning; collaborative editing; PII-sanitized copies for compliance; ML experimentation; offline/distributed workflows; agentic workflows. Addresses the problem that applying schema changes tends to be disruptive and offline even today. Relevant for dynamic ontology/KG systems that need continuous schema evolution without downtime.

summary: As of September 2026, dynamic ontology research has converged on several interconnected paradigms: (1) Ontology-as-a-Kernel (OaK) — treating ontology as an executable kernel coupling schema + typed reasoning functions for LLM agents, with judge-driven iterative refinement; (2) Closed-loop incremental KG construction (DIAL-KG) — Meta-Knowledge Base orchestrating dual-track extraction, governance adjudication, and schema evolution in a transactional loop with soft deprecation; (3) Dual-knowledge decoding (Evo-DKD) — parallel structured/unstructured decoder streams with dynamic gating for autonomous ontology evolution; (4) Dynamic self-evolving extraction (DySECT) — symbiotic closed loop where extraction populates a probabilistic KB that feeds back via prompt tuning/few-shot/fine-tuning; (5) Schema evolution with LLMs (DSE-RE, OntoEKG, SCOPE/SCION) — iterative schema induction from text, entailment-based hierarchy construction, and benchmark-driven evaluation; (6) Ontology change propagation (OntoRipple) — declarative propagation of 25 OWL change operations to RML mappings and SHACL shapes with dependency-ordered processing; (7) Temporal knowledge graphs (ATOM, Graphiti/Zep) — bi-temporal modeling (valid vs ingestion time), atomic fact decomposition, incremental updates with conflict resolution via temporal metadata; (8) Versioned memory graphs — formal belief revision semantics, git-backed versioning (Letta), immutable revisions with typed reasoning edges (Graph-Native Cognitive Memory), enterprise-grade auditability for regulatory compliance. The field is shifting from static ontology engineering to self-evolving, agent-integrated semantic infrastructure with formal governance.
